thread:
incident-bot: 🔴 INCIDENT DETECTED: GPU pool 'burst-eu-west-1' saturated, enqueue growth spike >3000, autoscaler hitting configured max replicas. Service: /v1/generate high latencies & elevated 429s. Pager fired.

oncall-ops: acked. joining bridge now — zoom.us/j/xxxxx and paging SREs. anyone on-call in eu? @alex.k @priya

alex.k: on it. hopping on bridge. started pulling metrics: queue length has been increasing steadily for ~18m, p50->p95 gap widening. looks like autoscaler didn't kick beyond 120 replicas due to max cap.

priya: I see the same. autoscaler event shows frequent scale attempts but rejected: "maxReplicasReached" in controller logs. we set max to 120 during cost-constraining rollout last quarter.

jamie: pushing recent replica-metrics:
```
max_replicas: 120
current_replicas: 120
enqueue_depth: 3247
avg_latency_tokens: 180ms -> 1.2s
throttled_requests_5m: 9.4%
errors_5m: 4.1% (429s mostly)
```

morgan: customer impact quick check: ~8% of all /generate traffic in eu-west. top affected customers by volume: acme-analytics, humanscale, appflux. cs-bot queued messages to CS for those customers.

rachel: tagging infra: allocation ceilings on our cloud account flagged some quota limits for ephemeral GPUs. I can request rapid increase but API is slow. We should enable fallback routing to lower-cost variants and reduce headroom.

samir: two parallel mitigations we can do immediately:
- bump autoscaler max to 240 (fast) and trigger scale.
- enable model-fallback route for non-enterprise customers to small-llama-7b which uses less GPU mem.
Which do we prioritize? both?

oncall-ops: prioritize quick wins: bump max then fallback routing. I'll take autoscaler patch.

alex.k: patching HPA config now. command:
```
kubectl -n production patch hpa/gpu-inference --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/maxReplicas","value":240}]'
```
Applying... -> PATCH ACCEPTED. HPA controller scheduled immediate scale.

jamie: after patch, controller log shows scale up events but pool provisioning from cloud provider is slow — warmup ~6-9m per node. we should also request emergency capacity.

rachel: filed emergency quota increase with provider with priority ticket #INC-8932. provider responded: "attempting to provision capacity, ETA 8-12m".

morgan: patching routing to fallback model for non-SLA traffic. snippet to update traffic-rule:
```
redwood route update /v1/generate --add-fallback small-llama-7b --match "!customer.sla:enterprise"
```

priya: enabling fallback now. will monitor error rate and latencies.

~6 minutes later

jamie: autoscaler scaled to 180 replicas; enqueue dropped from 3247 -> 900. 429s down to 1.2%.

samir: model-fallback uptake ~22% of incoming eu-west requests (non-enterprise). latency for those requests is acceptable (~600ms p95) and cost lower. overall system load reduced.

oncall-ops: good. still seeing some queue hotspots on particular shards. working with runtime team to redistribute KV cache affinity.

alex.k: temporary mitigation successful. initiating slow rollback of aggressive throttles. we should keep autoscaler max at 220 for next 12h to be safe.

priya: created a temporary policy to mark low-priority queues with TTL of 30s to reduce long-running requests.

cs-bot: CS notify: Sent targeted notifications to top impacted customers (acme-analytics, appflux) with current mitigation summary and ETA for full recovery.

morgan: customer impact summary for postmortem: 8% of eu-west traffic hit increased latencies; ~4% 429s at peak; resolved to <0.5% 429s after scaling + fallback. No data loss reported.

oncall-ops: closing live incident but leaving post-incident monitoring in place for 3h. creating postmortem doc and assigning action items.

-- POST-INCIDENT ACTIONS (from thread) --
- Alex K: remove legacy hard cap in autoscaler config and replace with workload-driven policy (due: 2026-04-01).
- Priya: add guardrail alert to flag sustained enqueue growth >1000 for >5m before hitting max replicas (due: 2026-03-22).
- Jamie: implement faster warm pool of standby GPUs in eu-west (low-cost reserved nodes) and run a test exercise (due: 2026-03-15).
- Rachel: validate cloud provider quota automation & escalate procedure; ensure emergency quotas pre-approved for +100 GPUs (due: 2026-03-10).
- Samir: implement automatic fallback to small models for non-SLA traffic when queue > threshold (due: 2026-03-18).
- Morgan/CS: follow-up customer outreach and prepare status page template for capacity incidents (due: 2026-03-12).

alex.k: adding notes to incident board, will attach logs and timeline. thanks everyone for fast response. :clap:

priya: we should run a tabletop this week to exercise the fallback + scale flow.

samir: agreed. will schedule and include runbook edits.

oncall-ops: incident closed — monitoring for 3h. if we see repeat enqueue surges, escalate to postmortem priority P1.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: burst-eu-west-1 pool enqueue normalized, 429s returned to baseline. Details in /incidents/5174623456-burst-pool-saturation-rapid-response postmortem (draft).
